{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RyM9mjVYKmUw4eQL8cDpuv","type":"tool_result","content":"=== sources/full_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\n# The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a\n# passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh\n=== sources/run_conformance.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n=== sources/setup_harness.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.\n#\n# Requires network access and a Go toolchain of at least 1.22 — the same floor\n# stack/go.md sets for the deliverable. The Go shipped by apt on Debian and\n# Ubuntu is frequently older and will fail; install the official tarball instead:\n#\n#     curl -sL https://go.dev/dl/go1.24.6.linux-amd64.tar.gz -o go.tgz\n#     sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go.tgz\n#     export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sh sources/setup_harness.sh              # install to $HOME/.local/bin\n#   GOBIN=/usr/local/bin sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nset -eu\n\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=v2.2.0\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}\"\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"error: no go toolchain on PATH; see the header of this script\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"go:      $(go version)\"\necho \"target:  ${GOBIN}/toml-test\"\necho \"version: ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${GOBIN}\"\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN}\" go install \\\n    \"github.com/toml-lang/toml-test/v2/cmd/toml-test@${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\necho\n\"${GOBIN}/toml-test\" version\n\ncase \":${PATH}:\" in\n    *\":${GOBIN}:\"*) ;;\n    *) echo\n       echo \"warning: ${GOBIN} is not on PATH. Add it, or export\"\n       echo \"         TOML_TEST=${GOBIN}/toml-test before running the suite.\" ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_contract.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_contract.sh — governed gates for boundaries not represented by one toml-test slice.\nset -eu\n\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_contract.sh <architecture|decoder>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\n\ncase \"$1\" in\n  architecture)\n    test -f go.mod\n    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then\n      echo \"go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    ;;\n  decoder)\n    go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    stage_dir=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    trap 'rm -rf \"$stage_dir\"' EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n    printf 'answer = 42\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/valid.json\" 2>\"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    python - \"$stage_dir/valid.json\" <<'PY'\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nwith open(sys.argv[1], encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n    decoded = json.load(stream)\nassert decoded == {\"answer\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"42\"}}\nPY\n\n    if printf 'answer = [\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/invalid.out\" 2>\"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"; then\n      echo \"malformed TOML exited successfully\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.out\"\n    test -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"\n    ;;\n  *)\n    echo \"unknown stage contract: $1\" >&2\n    exit 2\n    ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.\n#\n# Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder,\n# then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1. Exit status is the\n# verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run \"$1\"","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"329ef578-4c8b-46f3-8e73-53e587dfa5cf","uuid":"e9762a54-cc95-4b59-85a7-a7dfd2b2b4aa","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:06:24.817Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"=== sources/full_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Add it, or export\"\n       echo \"         TOML_TEST=${GOBIN}/toml-test before running the suite.\" ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_contract.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_contract.sh — governed gates for boundaries not represented by one toml-test slice.\nset -eu\n\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_contract.sh <architecture|decoder>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\n\ncase \"$1\" in\n  architecture)\n    test -f go.mod\n    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then\n      echo \"go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    ;;\n  decoder)\n    go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\n    stage_dir=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    trap 'rm -rf \"$stage_dir\"' EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n    printf 'answer = 42\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/valid.json\" 2>\"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/valid.err\"\n    python - \"$stage_dir/valid.json\" <<'PY'\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nwith open(sys.argv[1], encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n    decoded = json.load(stream)\nassert decoded == {\"answer\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"42\"}}\nPY\n\n    if printf 'answer = [\\n' | ./toml-decoder >\"$stage_dir/invalid.out\" 2>\"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"; then\n      echo \"malformed TOML exited successfully\" >&2\n      exit 1\n    fi\n    test ! -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.out\"\n    test -s \"$stage_dir/invalid.err\"\n    ;;\n  *)\n    echo \"unknown stage contract: $1\" >&2\n    exit 2\n    ;;\nesac\n=== sources/stage_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.\n#\n# Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder,\n# then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1. Exit status is the\n# verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run \"$1\"","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01RyM9mjVYKmUw4eQL8cDpuv","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) document() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdoc := map[string]any{}\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn doc, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c := p.src[p.pos]; c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r' {\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tkey, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, dup := doc[key]; dup {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", key)\n\t\t}\n\t\tdoc[key] = value\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() (string, map[string]any, error) {\n\tkey, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", key)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn key, value, nil\n}\n\n// key reads a bare key or a single-line quoted key. The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] Strings start with a quote;\n// everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn A nested table\n// is a table value; a key/value pair is the tagged map[string]any that value returns.\n// The two dynamic types differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table map[string]any\n\n// key reads a dotted key: one or more key parts joined by '.'. Spaces and tabs around\n// each part are ignored. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(doc table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tcur := doc\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, exists := cur[part]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tsub := table{}\n\t\t\tcur[part] = sub\n\t\t\tcur = sub\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsub, ok := next.(table)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", part)\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = sub\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps for the caller. A nested table\n// is a table value; a key/value pair is the tagged map[string]any that value returns.\n// The two dynamic types differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table map[string]any\n\n// key reads a dotted key: one or more key parts joined by '.'. Spaces and tabs around\n// each part are ignored. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key. Table headers are not\n// decoded yet, so a '[' is reported as a syntax error by the caller.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below doc, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(doc table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tcur := doc\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, exists := cur[part]\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tsub := table{}\n\t\t\tcur[part] = sub\n\t\t\tcur = sub\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsub, ok := next.(table)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", part)\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = sub\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps for the caller. Values are shared,\n// not copied, because each leaf is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t))\n\tfor k, v := range t {\n\t\tif sub, ok := v.(table); ok {\n\t\t\tout[k] = sub.export()\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout[k] = v\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":7,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":[" package toml"," ","-import \"strings\"","-"," // table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XbmWQorDLgARh3i7o9Dhbn","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"329ef578-4c8b-46f3-8e73-53e587dfa5cf","uuid":"e9cd4ab3-f426-434b-80b9-173d2aa5351e","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:12:02.202Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01XbmWQorDLgARh3i7o9Dhbn","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The rest of its rejection list is unchanged.\n- Internal nested tables use a separate type from tagged leaves, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\n\n**Files changed** (in the build directory; nothing in `sources/` or the protected paths was touched)\n- `internal/toml/toml.go`\n- `internal/toml/keys.go` (new)\n- `internal/toml/keys_test.go` (new)\n- `internal/toml/toml_test.go`\n- `cmd/toml-decoder/keys_test.go` (new)\n- `toml-decoder` (rebuilt binary; already tracked as modified)\n\nRESULT: FAILED\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- internal/toml/toml.go\n- internal/toml/keys.go\n- internal/toml/keys_test.go\n- internal/toml/toml_test.go\n- cmd/toml-decoder/keys_test.go\n- toml-decoder\n\nSUMMARY:\nImplemented bare, quoted, and dotted keys with redefinition checks in `internal/toml/keys.go`. All three declared key acceptance checks pass, and `go test -race` is green. Key-scoped toml-test run with comma-separated patterns: valid 18 passed / 10 failed, invalid 61 passed / 0 failed.
